newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland plans VAT refunds for tourists.
newsitem.headline: Poland plans VAT refunds for tourists.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry is working on a bill that would allow tourists leaving the country to get a refund of value added tax on goods bought in Poland, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.
"We would like the new regulation to take effect from next year..., possibly on one border to start with," he told a news conference. Poland levies 22 percent VAT on most products.

He said the bill was designed to curb the so-called shadow economy and tax evasion by companies. It will encourage small firms, seeking to boost sales, to declare themselves as VAT payers and come out of the grey untaxed zone, he said. @
"The budget will lose some revenue as a result of the regulation... but we should have more VAT payers," he said.
